analysis.title: JPM US Market Intelligence - Morning Briefing (November 9, 2026)
key_insights: Sales commentary, not research. Premarket: SPX +0.5%, NDX +0.4%, RTY +1.2%, WTI -98bps at $89.94, Gold +65bps at $4,097, 10Y at 4.866%, VIX at 23.62. Futures are higher as the tech trade stabilizes, while markets favor an ex-AI broadening trade, with EU outperformance as the example.

NVDA is down 4.4% premarket on 'honey pot risk' and is weighing on Semis, Memory and Mag7. Software leads tech, the other Mag7 names are higher, and pre-market action points to an 'Everything Rally' outside AI.

Last week SPX fell 2.7% (fourth straight weekly decline), NDX fell 5% and RTY fell 2%. The JPMPURE Momentum factor fell 5.6% (fifth straight weekly decline, 15.7% in total). AI baskets fell 18%+ and popular shorts were covered in a general de-risking.

Crude fell $13.29 (12.8%) last week on US/Iran deal optimism following the Blue Wave outcome. The 2Y yield fell 7.6bp, the 10Y 7.2bp and the 30Y 4.4bp as the curve bull flattened. USD rose on the week on Friday's gains.

Dubravko Lakos-Bujas reiterates a YE26 SPX target of 8,000 ($365 EPS at 21.9x), 8.4% above Friday's close. He frames the pullback as a de-leveraging event in AI and momentum names that began when liquidity thinned in late June, amplified by systematic, vol-control and buyside liquidations.

Dubravko's case that selling is far along: Momentum crowding reset from the 100th to the 76th percentile, levered ETF sales of ~$60bn Thursday and $35bn the prior Friday, CTAs flipped net short with maybe $50bn left to sell, dealer net gamma at the 12th percentile, $1.2T of announced buybacks, and QQQ RSI below 30, which has averaged a ~4% rally over the next five trading days.
Equity multiples have compressed ~4x since January and AI company multiples ~35% since May (Semis 52%, hyperscalers 14%, Memory 60%, Processing Units 50%), while earnings grew double digits.

Dubravko's trade ideas: long 12M momentum vs short 3M momentum, Low Vol less compelling after moving from the 0th to the 25th percentile (prefers Healthcare, then Utilities, then Staples if staying in Low Vol), AI upstream attractive after the positioning flush, and Consumer Cyclicals still challenged by affordability.

Catalysts named: Middle East developments, MegaCap IPOs, next month's ERCOT meeting (AI capex implications), and the December Fed meeting. Midterm elections are seen as a clearing event. Each $100B of extra capex adds ~$9 to 2027 S&P 500 EPS, so capex at ~$1.5T would add about $18 vs consensus.

Data center politics: Texas Governor-Elect Hinojosa says the state will move to protect citizens from data center energy and water costs, and her predecessor had halted new grid connections. Ohio Democrats broke the GOP supermajority. Feroli notes data center build jobs are ~165,000 over the past year, only 0.1% of employment, which may explain the backlash.

Labor and Fed: NFP beat expectations, initial claims hit a 52-week low, and announced job cuts on a 3-month average are down 52% YoY. JPM Economics keeps a December Fed hike as its call. Feroli forecasts October CPI at +0.25% MoM headline and +0.23% core, and PPI at +0.6% headline and +0.4% core.

Earnings (FactSet, 88% of SPX reported): blended EPS growth 31.4%, blended revenue growth 14.3%, margins 14.9%, all 11 sectors positive. EPS beats average 2.7% vs 7.5% and 8.0% 5- and 10-year averages, and the market is rewarding beats and punishing misses less than usual.

Middle East scenarios from JPM Commodity Trading: 50% chance of further strikes then a declaration that military action is over, and 50% chance diplomacy is given more time (a $4-5 decline in prices and a 7-10 point fall in volatility). The energy desk sees no chance of wider re-escalation this weekend.

Positioning Intelligence: HFs fell 1.6% on Thursday, the worst day since Apr 4, 2025, with a fourth straight day of de-grossing. Multi-Strat 20-day de-grossing is the largest outside Covid. HF net leverage is near 12-month lows and momentum exposure is near 3-year lows. Semis are the most net-sold group. A rebound is judged more likely than not, but the path is murky.

Futures positioning: clients bought the US long end (Ultra T-Bond 1wk change +1.9z), mostly short covering. Positioning is no longer stretched either way, so yield moves after the FOMC look like a toss-up driven by oil, AI-led growth and Fed guidance.

US Fixed Income Weekly: the desk looks for a 25bp Fed hike in December, sees risks skewed to front-end yields reversing higher, and stays neutral on duration. HY spreads widened 12bp to a YTD high of 375bp while leveraged loans tightened. The desk stays constructive on leveraged credit over 3 months. Treasury left coupon sizes unchanged and removed 'at least' from its guidance.

sector_views.rationale: Dubravko says the positioning flush created an attractive entry point. Hyperscalers have less near-term upside but medium-term room to re-rate, with tighter compute capacity supporting pricing power, margins and operating cash flow.

Affordability is a headwind tied to oil prices, borrowing costs and housing shortages. He sees longer-term value in Apparel, Restaurants and Retail vs Energy, and housing needs mortgage rates near 6.0% to see inflows.
Low Vol is less compelling after moving from the 0th to the 25th percentile. If staying with it, the best opportunity is Healthcare, then Utilities, then Staples.
Mkt Intel says Mag7 EPS is below SPX493 and median EU growth is outpacing US growth, 13% vs 12%, for the first time since 2024Q4, which could mean tactical EU outperformance once markets stabilize.

earnings_insights: FactSet, 88% of SPX reported: blended (actual plus forecast for unreported) revenue growth 14.3%, blended EPS growth 31.4%, profit margin 14.9%. All 11 sectors show positive revenue and earnings growth.

Reported EPS prints average 2.7% above estimates, below the 5-year average of 7.5% and 10-year average of 8.0%. From T-2 to T+2, beats gain 80bp vs a 90bp 5-year average and misses fall 1.1% vs a -3.1% 5-year average.

Dubravko and team estimate 2027 EPS growth of ~20%. Their YE26 target uses $365 EPS (forecast). Each $100B of capex adds ~$9 to 2027 S&P 500 EPS, so capex at ~$1.5T implies ~$18 vs consensus, adding 4-5% to 2027 EPS growth.
Mag7 EPS growth is below SPX493 growth, and median EU growth is 13% vs 12% for the US, the first EU lead since 2024Q4.
Companies reporting Nov 9 include CEG, KKR, OXY, TTD, TTWO, HIMS, MARA, RKLB and LCID. No consensus figures are given. NVDA is down 4.4% premarket on 'honey pot risk'.

macro_indicators.interpretation: CPI prints Nov 10. The fixed income desk's forecasts are above market pricing and may flatten the curve as markets focus on December and 2027 hike potential.
The desk forecasts core at 0.23% m/m and could support front-end inflation pricing, with five-year breakevens near 12-month lows.
PPI prints Nov 13 and adds to the inflation data risk for the curve this week.
Part of the inflation data this week that may further flatten the curve.
Labor conditions remain in good standing, initial claims reached a 52-week low, and the forward look on wage growth is higher, which may add inflation pressure.

macro_indicators.indicator: Professional, scientific and technical services jobs
macro_indicators.interpretation: Feroli says one month is not a trend but it is a glimmer of hope that AI-related job loss is far off.

macro_indicators.reading: 25bp hike expected at the December meeting (Dec 9)
macro_indicators.interpretation: JPM Economics and the fixed income desk both look for a December hike. Futures positioning suggests yield moves after the FOMC are a toss-up.
Dubravko's team estimate, alongside JPM Economics expecting trend-like US GDP growth with modest disinflation.

risk_factors: Further AI and momentum de-leveraging, with Semis the most sold group and AI multiples already down ~35% since May.
Data center backlash: Texas and Ohio politics, and 40% of planned US data center capacity in states wanting to pause (news link). Dubravko expects the headwinds to be less onerous than priced.
Middle East escalation or US withdrawal could send Brent to $105-110 within a week in one scenario.
Inflation and wages: a stronger labor market and wage outlook may create inflationary pressure, and the desks see risks to front-end yields reversing higher.
HF alpha could fall further. Earlier similar episodes in late February 2020 and late October 2018 were followed by further losses.
Credit: HY spreads at a YTD high of 375bp. Hyperscalers need more funding sources including equity, and AI capex funding is at risk from exogenous credit shocks.
CMBS exposure to data center moratoria and rent regulations.
vol_and_positioning: VIX at 23.62 premarket. Dealer net gamma imbalance is at the 12th percentile. Vol targeters' leverage fell from the 65th to the 30th percentile, with maybe $50bn left to sell, and CTAs flipped to net short.
Momentum crowding reset from the 100th to the 76th percentile. Long Momentum fell ~11% in October (~6 standard deviations), with Momentum L/S down ~40% from its peak.
Hedge funds fell 1.6% on Thursday (worst day since Apr 4, 2025, greater than a 3z decline) and are down about 1.8% MTD. Multi-Strat alpha is most negative in EMEA and Quants in North America.

A fourth straight day of ~1.5z de-grossing occurred Thursday, similar to late July and early August. Multi-Strat 20-day de-grossing is the largest outside Covid. After Multi-Strat 20-day gross flows first fell below the 5th percentile on Oct 27, alpha rose over the following 20 days in 9 of 10 cases.

HF net leverage fell ~4% over the week and is near 12-month lows. Eq L/S net leverage is at a 3-year low. Global momentum exposure is near 3-year lows. EMEA shorts covered at an extreme 3z level, last seen in late 2022.
US Tactical Positioning Monitor fell -1.7z over one week to the 20th percentile since 2015, but the 4-week change is -0.5z against a -1.5z trigger for an attractive set-up.
Semis are the clear group sold. HFs net sold Semis at a nearly 4z level over the past month, and 2-month and 3-month selling is around 4z, unseen in past data.

Futures: Ultra T-Bond 1wk change +1.9z (97th percentile of weekly changes since 2020), T-Bond +1.2z, but 4-week T-Bond is still -1.6z. Systematic investors remain net short at every point on the curve. China selling in A50 futures is at -3.4z (1wk), the bottom 1st percentile on 12-month positioning.
Gold: the share of clients net long fell to 56%, the lowest in a year and down from 87% in late August, with Systematic investors the main sellers. Ags are rolling over from highs on 9/1.
Rates vol: the interest rate derivatives desk recommends trading the vol surface and spread curve hedged to NDX moves, and keeps expiry curve steepeners and calendar spreads for forward vol.
geopolitical: US/Iran: crude fell 12.8% last week on deal optimism. President Trump said the US carried out 'minor strikes' on Iran as missiles hit Qeshm Island (news link). The MOU collapsed in June.

JPM Center for Geopolitics outlined three options: an 'Epic Fury 2.0' repeating spring targets, broader attacks on energy and civilian infrastructure, or a 'final blow' on a nuclear target. Washington has not used these options since June for fear of Iranian retaliation.

JPM Commodity Trading scenarios: 50% further strikes then a declaration that action is over (75% the US stays to secure Strait of Hormuz passage and keeps the blockade, 25% it withdraws), and 50% diplomacy gets more time.
US midterm results (the 'Blue Wave'): Texas Governor-Elect Hinojosa plans data center protections and Ohio Democrats broke the GOP supermajority. Dubravko sees the midterms as a clearing event.
US and China have agreed to extend the trade truce through January 20, 2027. APEC Economic Leaders Meeting is Nov 18-19 in Shenzhen and the G20 Summit is Dec 15-16 in Miami.
US Government funding deadline is Dec 11.

tension_points.bull_case: Dubravko says selling is far along: Momentum crowding reset to the 76th percentile, levered ETF exposure below January levels, $1.2T of buybacks, and QQQ RSI below 30. He keeps an 8,000 SPX target.
tension_points.bear_case: Multiples fell ~35% for AI names since May, hedge funds are still de-grossing, Semis are net sold at ~4z, and the US positioning monitor is not yet at an attractive set-up. Data center political backlash adds a headwind.
tension_points.what_invalidates: US TPM 4-week change is only -0.5z against a -1.5z trigger for an attractive set-up, and CTAs have maybe $50bn left to sell, so further selling would undercut the bull case.

tension_points.bull_case: The desks stay neutral on duration and see scope for breakevens to find a floor, with positioning no longer stretched.
tension_points.bear_case: Strong labor and wage data, CPI forecasts above market pricing and a December hike keep risks skewed to front-end yields reversing higher.
tension_points.what_invalidates: If equities find firmer footing, the Governments and Cross Sector desks would shift underweight the front end.

tension_points.bull_case: Diplomacy given more time would bring a $4-5 decline in prices and a 7-10 point fall in volatility through the week.
tension_points.bear_case: Further strikes with a US withdrawal would see Brent fall ~$4 then recover to $105-110 within a week.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A US withdrawal after declaring mission complete would send Brent to $105-110 within a week, per the scenario analysis.
